purpose: Fourth S4 conflict-closure batch implementing the reviewed P12-P16 families. Four distinct conservative dependency-lock aliases cover AMP and bridge/rollup system families without pretending they are generic tokens/routers; P16 is promoted to the existing cw721-drop family after representative minimal-proxy/implementation review. All mappings remain candidate-only until exact family gates and later selector/native-readiness gates pass.

decisions.mapping_basis: Official AMP documentation and the verified Ethereum source for 0xff2081...95c2 show that AMP is not a plain ERC20: it adds per-holder partitions, partition allowances/operators, collateral-manager registration, ERC1820 transfer hooks, and partition strategies. Because the frozen S4 owner-level review exposes no selector narrow enough to justify a cw20-base subset, map the runtime family to the dedicated amp-partition-collateral-lock alias. The alias is deliberately conservative: one independent owner-scoped singleton dependency preserves every within-owner conflict without claiming exact AMP storage keys or EVM behavior. Review evidence is checked in as evaluation/vegeta/s4-fourth-batch-review-evidence.v1.json#p12-amp.
decisions.semantic_notes: Do not reinterpret this as cw20-base semantic equivalence. The family-level lock is an explicit conservative dependency abstraction; selector-level/native-execution readiness remains separately fail-closed.

decisions.identity_hint: Linea L1 Message Service / LineaRollup family
decisions.mapping_basis: The exact owner is publicly identified as Linea's L1 Message Service/LineaRollup. Frozen S4 directly observes selector 0x4165d6dd, and public transaction/explorer evidence identifies calls with this selector as Finalize Blocks. Linea's reviewed source describes global rollup/message-service state for block finalization and cross-chain messaging. Map the family to linea-rollup-lock, an independent owner-scoped singleton dependency for the observed global mutation class. This preserves conservative conflicts while making no claim about proof verification, per-block root layout, message Merkle structures, or EVM state equivalence. Review evidence is checked in as evaluation/vegeta/s4-fourth-batch-review-evidence.v1.json#p13-linea.
decisions.semantic_notes: 0x4165d6dd is translated only to the conservative global dependency guard; later selector-semantic validation remains authoritative.

decisions.identity_hint: ZKsync Era L1 DiamondProxy/main-chain contract family
decisions.mapping_basis: Official ZKsync documentation identifies 0x324000...0324 as the Era L1 DiamondProxy/main chain contract. Frozen S4 directly observes selector 0xeb672419; official SDK bindings identify it as requestL2Transaction(address,uint256,bytes,uint256,uint256,bytes[],address). The request path mutates chain-global priority-operation/mailbox state across diamond facets, so it is not mapped to a token/router family. zksync-l1-system-lock conservatively serializes that owner-scoped state-touch class without modeling facet routing, queue contents, proof state, or EVM execution equivalence. Review evidence is checked in as evaluation/vegeta/s4-fourth-batch-review-evidence.v1.json#p14-zksync.
decisions.semantic_notes: The DiamondProxy storage namespace is the native instance namespace; the observed requestL2Transaction class maps only to the conservative singleton dependency guard.

decisions.mapping_basis: The exact owner is publicly identified as the Arbitrum One L1 Bridge. Official Nitro Bridge/IBridge source defines delayed and sequencer message accumulators/counts, allowed inbox/outbox state, active outbox, rollup linkage, and execution state; current explorer activity also shows delayed-message enqueue calls reaching this bridge. Because the frozen owner summary does not expose a selector narrow enough for a more granular alias, map the runtime family to arbitrum-bridge-lock, an independent owner-scoped singleton dependency. This conservatively preserves bridge-global conflict structure without modeling accumulator contents, ETH escrow, low-level call effects, or EVM state equivalence. Review evidence is checked in as evaluation/vegeta/s4-fourth-batch-review-evidence.v1.json#p15-arbitrum.
decisions.semantic_notes: Family-level bridge dependency classification only. Selector-level execution remains fail-closed until separately reviewed.

decisions.mapping_basis: Frozen S4 groups 31 storage owners under this identical runtime-code family. Public explorer/source review of representative owners 0x0d049a...43a46, 0x12dd66...ae221, and 0xc374a2...e9579c identifies ERC721 collections implemented as minimal proxies to the same Archetype implementation 0x563fbc5181a6ca2970e94152c9969f19d0e37ad3. The implementation exposes ERC721 ownership/approval/transfer plus mint flows. Reuse cw721-drop for those ownership/approval/sequential-mint dependency classes; collection-specific sale, affiliate, withdrawal, metadata, and admin state is not inferred and unsupported selectors remain opaque. Review evidence is checked in as evaluation/vegeta/s4-fourth-batch-review-evidence.v1.json#p16-archetype-erc721.
decisions.semantic_notes: Family-wide reuse is justified by identical minimal-proxy runtime plus representative exact-owner implementation checks. This is dependency-family reuse, not application state equivalence.
